clue.text: European tax cut backed by Switzerland

indicators.note: backed by means the next piece stands behind, following on
cut means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a duty is a tax, as on imports
CH is the international code for Switzerland (Confoederatio Helvetica)

explanation.surface: A news item about a European levy being trimmed with Swiss support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' takes the last letter off DUTY, leaving DUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from the Netherlands is a European, so the nationality word fits.

clue.text: Enthusiasm shown by cartoonist making a bomb?

definitions.meaning: a bug is an enthusiasm, and a cartoonist's is for idle sketching
the V-1 flying bomb of the Second World War had this nickname

explanation.surface: An artist producing a bomb with great enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname for the German V-1 flying bomb that hit London in 1944.

clue.text: One working high up, labourer lacking oxygen

indicators.note: lacking says something is missing from the word

parts.note: a toiler is someone who labours
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A worker on a mountain short of breath.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone laying slates on a roof works at height.

clue.text: Accumulating advertising space

definitions.meaning: a large board for posters beside a road

explanation.surface: Building up billboard space.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockpiling is accumulating; the British word for a billboard is also this.

clue.text: Angry about multi-talented artist?

parts.note: cross means angry
over can mean about, as in arguing over something

explanation.surface: Someone getting angry about a performer who does too many things at once.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer who moves between genres, such as classical to pop, is called by this term; the question mark flags the loose description.

clue.text: Form of punishment, you say, for a killer

indicators.note: you say signals that the word for the punishment is spoken

parts.note: a cane was used to beat pupils

explanation.surface: Choosing a punishment for a murderer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Adam's son slew his brother Abel, the first murderer.

clue.text: Likely place of kings and queens

definitions.meaning: court cards are printed on playing cards

explanation.surface: A probable royal residence.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means probable; literally, kings and queens are found printed on playing cards.

clue.text: Trailer: form of publicity during performance

indicators.note: during puts the advert in the middle of the show

parts.note: a show is a performance
an ad is an advertisement

explanation.surface: A film trailer is shown as an advert during a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trailer' looks like a film preview, but it means someone who follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tails a person is a follower or trailer, as a detective does.

clue.text: Old actor, not an evil sort

indicators.note: sort as a verb means arrange, so these letters are put in order anew

explanation.surface: A veteran actor who is not a villainous type.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolph, the silent-film star of the 1920s, was a famous screen idol of old.

clue.text: Argumentative participant in boating event?

definitions.meaning: taken as one who rows, rhyming with cows, i.e. quarrels

explanation.surface: A quarrelsome crew member at a regatta.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a whimsical noun for one who quarrels.
explanation.definitionFit: One who rows a boat takes part in a regatta; one who rows (quarrels) argues.

clue.text: Bourbon supporter's poor relations

indicators.note: poor suggests the word relations is badly put together, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A royalist's struggling family members.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of the Orléans branch of the French royal house, itself a cadet line of the Bourbons, backed that claim to the throne.

clue.text: Permit sickly-looking son to leave

indicators.note: to leave says the son goes out of the word

parts.note: sallow describes a sickly, yellowish complexion

explanation.surface: Letting a pale, unwell boy go home.
explanation.definitionFit: To permit something is to let it happen; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: East of Los Angeles reconstruct city of Texas

indicators.note: east of in an across clue puts the next piece to the right of the city

parts.note: to redo something is to reconstruct it

explanation.surface: A plan to rebuild a Texan city somewhere east of Los Angeles.
explanation.definitionFit: Laredo is a border city in southern Texas, on the Rio Grande.

clue.text: Anti-Brexiteer more confused by an embodiment of sovereignty?

indicators.note: confused tells us the letters of more are jumbled

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the monarch, who embodies sovereignty

explanation.surface: A Brexit opponent baffled by the Queen, a nod to sovereignty debates.
explanation.walkthrough: ER = the Queen, Elizabeth Regina; 'confused' turns MORE into REMO.
explanation.definitionFit: A derogatory nickname for someone who kept complaining about the UK leaving the EU, i.e. an opponent of the referendum result.

clue.text: Kind of shock about vandal regularly breaking into parts of port

indicators.note: breaking into puts the pieces inside the harbour areas

parts.note: docks are areas of a harbour
re means about, concerning

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of vandal

explanation.surface: A vandal breaking into the docks causes a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' keeps ADL, the even letters. 'Shock' looks like a jolt, matching the vandal story, but here it is a mass of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock of hair can be matted ropes, as in Rastafarian style.

clue.text: Something to make sandwiches or toast for a Cockney?

definitions.meaning: a wholemeal loaf used for making sandwiches
in Cockney rhyming slang the phrase rhymes with dead, and toast is slang for doomed or dead

explanation.surface: Making sandwiches or toast, with a Londoner's twist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toast' looks like grilled bread, matching the sandwiches, but here means done for. Cockney rhyming slang is London East End slang where a phrase stands for the word it rhymes with.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholemeal loaf is used for sandwiches; and in rhyming slang the phrase means dead, as does slang toast.

clue.text: Public line about Henry's defeat

indicators.note: about here means on, so the line comes after the unit

parts.note: overt means open, public
H is the symbol of the henry, the unit of inductance
a row is a line

explanation.surface: A public line about a king Henry's downfall.
explanation.definitionFit: Toppling a ruler or government is its defeat.

clue.text: Lacking energy? That's a problem for a walker

definitions.text: That's a problem for a walker
definitions.meaning: an uneven gait from an injured leg troubles anyone walking

explanation.surface: A tired hiker with a sore leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means floppy or feeble; the noun is a lame gait that hampers walking.

clue.text: Tapes sent for review? That could be perfect

indicators.note: for review suggests the tapes are gone through again and the letters reworked

explanation.surface: Sending recordings off for critique, hoping they're flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perfect' is the grammatical tense, as in 'has done'.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the perfect is one form of the past, so it is an example.

clue.text: Still unlikely to arouse feeling

explanation.surface: A dull, static scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Motionless things are still; work that fails to stir emotion is also described so.

clue.text: Cultivated part of flower garden in retirement

indicators.note: in retirement says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone who took up growing flowers after retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft defined 'Cultivated part', but 'part of' is the hiding signal; the definition is 'Cultivated' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of raise or cultivate a plant, as a gardener does.

clue.text: Cool fellow tries Spanish dances

parts.note: to fan someone is to cool them
Dan is a man's name, standing for any fellow
goes means attempts, as in has a go

explanation.surface: A laid-back man attempts some flamenco-style dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively Spanish courtship dance in triple time, here in the plural.

clue.text: Check membership fee needs renewing?

parts.note: a sub is a subscription
due means owed, as a fee is when it must be renewed

explanation.surface: Checking whether a club subscription is up for renewal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' looks like a verb meaning inspect; it means restrain.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to restrain or curb it, synonyms of quell.

clue.text: What made-to-measure clothes should do, every now and then

definitions.meaning: tailored garments ought to sit on the body completely and well

explanation.surface: A tailor's promise about bespoke garments that only occasionally holds.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words to get the tailoring sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Read whole, it means intermittently, in irregular bursts, which matches every now and then.

clue.text: Not getting up after endless fun in bed

indicators.note: after puts the reversed word behind the first piece
endless means the word loses its final letter
getting up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Lazing in bed after the fun is over.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese-style mattress used as a bed, often on a low frame.

clue.text: Pet tearing about in Tesco's

indicators.note: tearing about pictures frantic movement, so the letters of the shop name are mixed

explanation.surface: A dog running wild in a Tesco supermarket.
explanation.walkthrough: Tesco is a large British supermarket chain; its letters with the S rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, pet means to pamper or fuss over, a synonym.

clue.text: Long story by new French writer

parts.note: a saga is a long story

explanation.surface: A French novelist's lengthy new tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Françoise, author of Bonjour Tristesse, was a French novelist.

clue.text: Start to produce amateur drama

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: lay means non-professional, amateur

explanation.surface: Beginning to stage an amateur theatre piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a stage work, a synonym for a theatrical piece.

clue.text: After half-time, Liverpool player is exhausted

indicators.note: after puts the footballer behind the first piece
half says only the first half of the word time is kept

parts.note: Liverpool FC play in red and are nicknamed the Reds

explanation.surface: A footballer flagging in the second half of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-time' looks like the break in a match; it is half of TIME, TI. Liverpool FC are known as the Reds.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired and exhausted are synonyms for being worn out.

clue.text: Having recourse to language used in California (North)

indicators.note: used in says the language piece goes inside the others

parts.note: lingo is informal for a language

explanation.surface: Slang spoken in northern California.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw upon a resource, as in drawing on reserves, means having recourse to it.

clue.text: State's fresh milk supplier?

parts.note: new means fresh
a Jersey is a breed of dairy cow

explanation.surface: A US state's dairy cow producing fresh milk.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the original thirteen US states, on the east coast.

clue.text: Short chap, namely a character in fairy tales

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: gent is short for gentleman, a chap
i.e. (id est) means namely

explanation.surface: A small man, like a figure in a fairy story.
explanation.definitionFit: The spirit of the lamp in Aladdin is a classic fairy-tale figure.
